subject: Renewal conversation: stability impact and proposed commitment
messages:
From: Anika Rao <anika@fintechcorp.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:14:22 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion: incident impact & SLA options

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the partnership — we’re approaching our contract renewal at the end of September and I wanted to flag the recent stability blips over the last three weeks. We saw two incidents that materially impacted tail latency for our payment authorization flows (spikes to 1.8s p95 from a baseline of ~220ms). That caused a handful of degraded customer experiences and triggered our incident playbook.

Procurement has asked that we document the impact and understand what options Redwood has to both remediate and offer a stronger SLO commitment at renewal. Specifically they want: 1) a clear remediation plan with timelines, 2) whether there’s a short-term uplift (pilot) toward a dedicated/premium tier for the next 90 days, and 3) what commercial terms (credits, SLA language) you’d consider.

Attached is our internal incident summary (incident_report_aug09.pdf) — not exhaustive but should help. Can we schedule a 30-minute call to walk through a concrete proposal we can take to procurement? 

Best,
Anika Rao
Head of Platform Ops
FinTechCorp

---
Attachment: incident_report_aug09.pdf (PDF, 84KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Rao <anika@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 11:03:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: incident impact & SLA options

Anika — thank you for the note and the incident report. I’m really sorry this impacted your authorization flows; I recognize how sensitive that is for FinTechCorp.

We’ve already begun a postmortem across serving/runtime and networking to correlate the spikes (prelim finding: a cross-tenant KV-cache invalidation event + transient autoscaler jitter during a high-concurrency window). I’ve attached our early investigation artifacts (investigation_notes_aug09.zip).

Short answers to your asks:
- Remediation plan & timeline: we can commit to a two-week code/config stabilization sprint (detailed items below) and an operational runbook update.
- Short-term uplift: we can provision a 90-day Dedicated Pilot (isolated GPU pool + reserved throughput) that reduces noisy-neighbor risk and gives you SLOs closer to 99.95 uptime and improved tail latency.
- Commercial terms: for expedited renewal we can offer a one-time service credit tied to the incident impact window and an SLA addendum for the pilot period.

If that sounds like a starting point, can we do a call tomorrow at 10am PT? I’ve looped Ben (serving runtime lead) and Sean (commercial lead) so they can present technical mitigations and the commercial term set.

Proposed quick remediation checklist (high level):
- Patch autoscaler debounce logic + add safety cap on burst scale actions (3 business days)
- Fix KV-cache invalidation path + add defensive caching fallback (5 business days)
- Add prefix-level KV caching for the authorization flow (8 business days)
- Validation run & short load test on the Dedicated Pilot (10–12 business days)

Next steps: confirm call time and we’ll bring a short deck and a concrete SLA addendum draft.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Thanks, Kimberly — 10am PT tomorrow works. I’ve added procurement in copy; they’ll want a few concrete numbers to assess the commercial ask.

A couple of clarifying requests for the call so procurement can prep:
- Can you outline the specific SLO language you’d propose for the 90-day Dedicated Pilot (availability %, latency p95 target for auth flow)?
- What would the pilot pricing differential look like and can you indicate the expected token/throughput headroom?
- For the one-time credit: are you proposing a fixed $ amount, a % of the monthly invoice, or credits tied to incident duration?

Procurement also asked that we share a short questionnaire ahead of time — I’ve attached it (procurement_questions_fintechcorp.xlsx). If you can complete the key fields and bring numbers to the call, that will speed sign-off.

See you tomorrow.

-Anika

---
Attachment: procurement_questions_fintechcorp.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: incident impact & SLA options

Anika — great talking with you and procurement this morning. Per our call, here’s the agreed near-term path we’ll capture in the renewal amendment and pilot statement of work: 

1) 90-day Dedicated Pilot (FTC-Pilot-90):
- Provisioning: isolated GPU pool with reservation for FinTechCorp (target throughput: 2x your current 99th percentile requests; we’ll baseline in the first 48 hours)
- SLOs for pilot: 99.95% availability (monthly) and p95 latency <= 280ms for the authorization endpoint when routed to the pilot pool
- Monitoring: shared dashboard + 15-minute paging for severity-1 events

2) Credit structure for the recent incidents:
- One-time credit equivalent to 20% of a single monthly invoice for August 2027, applied at renewal as a prorated credit (will appear on the first renewal invoice)

3) Remediation & timeline (as discussed):
- Autoscaler debounce patch: target completion in 3 business days from 2027-08-11
- KV-cache hardening + fallback: target completion in 6 business days
- Validation load test on pilot: within 10 business days of pilot activation

4) Commercial terms & next steps:
- Pilot pricing: mid-point between Hosted and Dedicated list pricing; we’ll submit a line-item in DocuSign for the pilot + SLA addendum (link: https://docusign.com/FT-2027-1147-proposal).
- Expected lead time to spin up pilot: 48–72 hours after countersignature and PO.
- We’ll deliver a short amendment draft by EOD tomorrow and Ben will provide a one-page technical appendix for procurement.

Please reply to confirm and we’ll circulate the DocuSign. We’ll also note the internal deal id: FTC-2027-1147 for tracking.

Thanks again — we’re committed to getting this stabilized and to a renewal that matches the reliability bar FinTechCorp expects.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Cc: Ben Carter (serving runtime), Sean Gallagher (Commercial)
